thread.title: Here's why Coca-Cola is muscling into the coffee-shop business in a big way

author: morningstar.com
title: Here's why Coca-Cola is muscling into the coffee-shop business in a big way
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
To get through this last workday before the long weekend, Coke's management just ordered up a whole lotta coffee.
Those big shots in Atlanta (KO)plan to buy British coffee-shop chain Costa (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/coke-to-buy-uk-coffee-chain-costa-for-51-bln-2018-08-31) for $5.1 billion, taking it over from Whitbread (WTB.LN) , a U.K. FTSE 100 component that has been jolted higher by the news.
What's the deal with this deal?
Coke, "like a lot of its peers, is looking to diversify away from its core business of sugary drinks, an area that has been increasingly attracting government ire due to a rising global obesity problem," says Michael Hewson, chief market analyst at CMC Markets UK, for our call of the day.
A growing number of U.S. cities, for example, have levied special taxes on sodas (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-seattle-sodatax/seattle-to-become-latest-u-s-city-to-tax-sugary-drinks-idUSKBN18X09T) and other sugary beverages.
Hewson warns that the coffee business is "extremely competitive," and he notes that the acquisition follows PepsiCo's (PEP)move to branch out in a different way with the agreement earlier this month to buy home-carbonation company SodaStream (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pepsis-sodastream-acquisition-wont-solve-its-biggest-problem-fewer-people-are-drinking-soda-2018-08-20)(SODA) . (Campbell Soup's (CPB)new strategic direction, meanwhile, is to get out of fresh food (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/is-campbell-soup-making-a-bad-decision-to-sell-its-fresh-food-business-2018-08-30).)
See:Pepsi will buy SodaStream, in extended shift away from sugary drinks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pepsi-will-buy-sodastream-in-extended-shift-away-from-sugary-drinks-2018-08-20)
Coke has jumped on the chance to "gain an attractive brand with a fast-growing global presence," writes Neil Wilson, Markets.com's chief market analyst.
The seller of Sprite and Powerade seems to think "this is the ideal way into a frothy market that it's maybe missed out on so far," Wilson adds.
Costa, a rival to Starbucks (SBUX)in the U.K., has more than 2,400 coffee shops in its home country, along with more than 1,400 retail outlets in other nations. It also sells coffee in grocery stores and gas stations.
Is this big trouble for Starbucks? Traders seem only somewhat concerned at the moment, with the Seattle company's shares down 1.6% in premarket trading.
Coke has ventured into coffee before, including acquiring a minority stake in once-hot Keurig Green Mountain (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/keurigs-buyout-turns-cokes-1-billion-loss-into-a-profit-2015-12-07). That company is now owned by an investor group led by JAB Holding (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/keurig-sale-comes-as-its-products-have-cooled-in-last-2-years-2015-12-07).
Don't miss:Coke's Costa Coffee deal doesn't appear cheap (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/coca-colas-costa-coffee-deal-doesnt-appear-cheap-2018-08-31)
Key market gauges
Futures for the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 are pulling back, after the Dow , S&P and Nasdaq Composite lost ground yesterday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-futures-flat-ahead-of-labor-day-major-indexes-set-for-strong-week-and-month-2018-08-31).
The three gauges are on track for weekly advances of 0.8% to 1.8% as of Thursday's close, along with August gains of 2.3% to 5.5%, with one day left in the month.
European (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-fall-as-trade-uncertainty-spikes-again-2018-08-31)and Asian markets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-fall-as-trump-pushes-more-tariffs-against-china-2018-08-30) have largely been seas of red, and analysts are blaming news that President Donald Trump could push forward soon with tariffs against China. Gold is higher, while oil and the dollar index are lower. Bitcoin is trading around $6,900.
See the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-futures-flat-ahead-of-labor-day-major-indexes-set-for-strong-week-and-month-2018-08-31) for the latest action.

If the bullish moves hold, shares ought to notch a fresh all-time high today. They've more than doubled over the past 12 months, and bulls are loving it:
(https://twitter.com/JeffMacke/status/1035260311727566848)
The buzz
Warren Buffett says Apple (AAPL)shouldn't buy (Berkshire%20Hathaway) Tesla (TSLA) .
"Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies are useless," says the latest issue (https://www.economist.com/leaders/2018/08/30/bitcoin-and-other-cryptocurrencies-are-useless?fsrc=scn/fb/te/bl/ed/bitcoinandothercryptocurrenciesareuselessshowmethemoney) of The Economist magazine. "For blockchains, the jury is still out."
Trump news: The president has threatened to withdraw from the WTO (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-threatens-to-pull-us-from-wto-may-link-capital-gains-taxes-to-inflation-2018-08-30) and rejected the European Union's recent offer to drop tariffs on American cars. Plus, he's expected to sign an executive order (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-to-issue-executive-order-on-potential-retirement-savings-changes-2018-08-30) today on potential retirement-savings changes.
Smith & Wesson parent America Outdoor Brands Corp (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/smith-wesson-maker-aobc-stock-soars-15-after-earnings-beat-2018-08-30).(AOBC)looks on track for a big up day after its earnings late yesterday, while Nutanix (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nutanix-shares-fall-after-hours-as-wider-than-expected-loss-forecast-2018-08-30)(NTNX)and Ulta Beauty (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ulta-beauty-stock-falls-after-earnings-include-forecast-miss-2018-08-30)(ULTA)appear headed in the other direction.
Shortly after the opening bell, watch for a reading on Chicagoland's business conditions as well as a figure for consumer sentiment.

At least seven people were killed (https://abc7.com/at-least-7-dead-in-crash-of-greyhound-bus-heading-to-ie-la/4102022/) and dozens injured in a crash in New Mexico involving an LA-bound Greyhound bus and a big rig.
European Union boss Jean-Claude Juncker is promising to end (https://www.dw.com/en/eu-to-stop-changing-the-clocks-juncker-pledges/a-45300586) that business of "fall back, spring forward" with clocks in EU countries: "The people want it, we'll do it."
The Quote:
"If there were ever a moment for us to talk and sit down and reflect about who we are, where we came from and where we're going, this weekend should give us that moment."--Texas Christian University assistant dean Ron Pitcock is Quote: d in an AP essay (https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory/ap-essay-aretha-franklin-john-mccain-1960s-57521109) that says memorial services for Aretha Franklin and John McCain ought to inspire some national soul-searching.
The essay also says Franklin and McCain "exit the stage together in an American moment not unlike the period when each emerged. Fifty years after the cataclysmic year of 1968, today we are in a similar period of upheaval and polarization -- a time when American society's foundational pillars are being questioned and people of all political persuasions are deeply angry and uncertain about the nation's path."
